purpose: Test whether typical rhythm patterns learned from original GMD MIDI can improve downbeat candidate selection on the three simpler project songs without modifying kick/snare events.

source_notes.official_gmd: Google Magenta Groove MIDI Dataset MIDI-only; original MIDI notes used directly. Kick=36, snare=37/38/40 per official mapping.
source_notes.mirror: zharry29/drums-with-llm data_midi contains the original MIDI files copied into train/dev/test splits per that repository README.
source_notes.invalidated_prior_experiment: Earlier gpt3_*.jsonl-derived text experiment is invalid for this purpose because the repository's midi_to_text.py and text_to_midi.py use inconsistent six-column primary-note orders. Those derived-text results must not be used as evidence.

heldout_sample.note: Single global template is unstable across mixed genres; not suitable as replacement.

multi_pattern_nearest_neighbor.note: Multiple prototypes improve representation but are still unstable on nanairo/ray.

direct_downbeat_classifier.feature: 4-bar kick/snare 16th-position occupancy; positive=correct bar rotation, negatives=1/2/3 beat rotations

decision.rationale: The current selector is correct on all three songs. GMD direct classifiers are training-sample-sensitive and would regress nanairo/ray in two of three independent batches.
decision.next_hypothesis: Use a much larger original-GMD training set with explicit genre/pattern mixture or bagged ensemble, and only accept a learned prior when held-out calibration is strong. Keep acoustic snare-contrast evidence dominant.
